content.text:
**Clarity — Letter A.** A is organized under plain-language headings that track the way a client reads: how it did, what we changed, what it costs. It also translates its own jargon: the benchmark is glossed as "global stocks and US bonds held at our glide path target weights," and the fee change is tied back to the parents' own May request rather than left as "breakpoint purposes." B collapses everything into four dense paragraphs, states the index return with no explanation of what the index is, and leaves "aggregate your accounts for breakpoint purposes" unexplained. B also writes "our cash position," which blurs whose account this is.

**Tone — Letter A.** The tone notes ask for a direct answer to Nils's question about holding 70% equities five years out. A answers it: it names Nils, calls the question fair, explains that the equity target steps down every year automatically, and makes the reassuring point that the first tuition dollars are out of the market entirely and sitting in Treasuries dated to when they are needed. B only gestures at the question — "This adjustment aligns with your question in May" — which acknowledges a worried parent without resolving the worry. B's register is also more boilerplate ("We are pleased to share," "wish to discuss your financial goals further"), and framing a fee reduction the clients themselves requested as firm good news reads slightly self-congratulatory. A's "Warm regards" and "call if you would like to talk any of this through" fit parents planning for a 13-year-old better than B's arms-length "your son Mateo."

**Overall — Letter A**, and not because it is longer; its extra words are doing the specific work of answering the question the household actually asked.

input.reason: Clarity: A uses plain-language headings (how it performed / what we changed / fee change) and glosses its own jargon — the benchmark is explained as global stocks and US bonds at glide path target weights, and the fee change is tied to the parents' own May request. B is four dense paragraphs, cites the comparison index without saying what it is, leaves 'breakpoint purposes' unexplained, and says 'our cash position,' which blurs ownership of the account. Tone: the tone notes require a direct answer to Nils's question about 70% equities with five years to college. A answers it — names Nils, explains the target steps down automatically each year, and reassures that the first-year tuition money is out of the market and in maturity-matched 2031 Treasuries. B merely notes the adjustment 'aligns with your question,' acknowledging the concern without resolving it. B is also more boilerplate ('We are pleased to share,' 'discuss your financial goals further'), frames a client-requested fee cut as firm good news, and 'your son Mateo' reads distant. A's warmth and open invitation to call suit parents planning for a 13-year-old. Length was not a factor; A's additional text is doing the specific job of answering the household's question.
